profile.name: Vins
profile.lede: A gently satirical line on Indian life, drawn in ink and watercolour. Political pocket cartoons for Himmat, the first Indian contributing cartoonist at Reader's Digest, shown in museums across Europe.

portraits.alt: Black and white portrait of Vijay Narain Seth, bearded and wearing glasses
Colour close-up portrait of Vijay Narain Seth smiling

about.heading: Humane, gently satirical work on the foibles of Indian life
about.pull: He regarded the veteran cartoonist Mario Miranda as his mentor.
about.bio:
Vijay Narain Seth, known by his pen name Vins, graduated from the Sir J. J. School of Fine Arts in Mumbai in 1968. While still a student he walked across to the Times of India office, almost next door, to watch Mario Miranda at work, and he began freelancing for Caravan and Himmat magazines.

He was the political cartoonist of the weekly Himmat from 1965 to 1981, drawing the pocket cartoon Chalta Hai every week and, from 1969, two further cartoons with national and international comment. Later he freelanced on science, computers, business and social issues.

He travelled widely in Europe and met leading graphic artists, among them the French cartoonist André François, whom he counted as an influence. His work was shown in cartoon festivals and exhibitions across Europe and Asia.

works.alt: Watercolour cartoon of three cheerful graduates in suits and a sari, tossing mortarboards trailing plug cords, with computers on a desk behind them
Watercolour cartoon of a man in a dark suit presenting a bouquet to a smiling woman, with an Indian flag and a French flag on the flowers
Watercolour cartoon of a lively group carrying trays and goblets of sweets, dancing across a yellow background with pink hearts
Watercolour cartoon of a man asleep on a table donating blood, while a nurse and announcer award a number 115 rosette and a queue with haloes waits behind
Watercolour cartoon of a speaker at a lectern dreaming of a mother and baby, while a smiling audience watches a large portrait on a banner

career.title: Born Vijay Narain Seth
career.text: Born on 10 March. Works under the pen name Vins.

career.title: Political cartoonist, Himmat weekly
career.text: Draws the weekly pocket cartoon Chalta Hai. From 1969 he adds two more cartoons commenting on national and international affairs.

career.title: Graduates from Sir J. J. School of Fine Arts, Mumbai
career.text: Already freelancing for Caravan and Himmat as a student.

career.title: Science Today
career.text: Contributes to the Times of India science publication.

career.title: First Indian contributing cartoonist, Reader's Digest India
career.text: Joins the Indian edition when Rahul Singh is chief editor. Later freelances for Business India, Business World and the Indian Express group's business publications.

career.title: Treffpunkt, Zurich
career.text: Invited to contribute cartoons to the fortnightly edited by Heidi Rudolf. He also drew for the Swiss satirical weekly Nebelspalter.

career.title: The Penguin Book of Indian Cartoons
career.text: His work is included in the anthology.

career.title: International festivals and exhibitions
career.text: Prizes in Edinburgh (1990), Berne (1996) and Taejon (1997), with exhibitions in Europe, and in Japan in 1998.

career.title: Died on 26 June, aged 70
career.text: His cartoons remain in museum collections in Switzerland and Turkey.
